limitations.finite: Finite nonempty rectangular data; generic <=10000rows,128columns,1Mcells; fit additionally<=2000rows,<=16features,2..200groups. Exact signed group IDs abs<=2^53-1. Parameters<=16384finite doubles.
limitations.identification: Automatic unpenalized intercept; full-rank standardized fixed design; n>features+2; >=2groups with repeat observations. Both Bernoulli classes required; allzero Poisson rejected. A fitted-tolerance-independent bounded LP rejects Bernoulli complete/quasi separation and Poisson zero-count recession directions. Numerical LP reduced-cost/pivot tolerance1e-12,positive summed-improvement threshold1e-10,feasibility1e-8; ambiguous/work/iteration failures reject. Extremely near-degenerate finite-MLE existence remains a numerical assessment,not exact arithmetic. Guard-bound hits cannot report convergence.
limitations.preprocessing: Fit-only origin+mean-offset/population-scale feature normalization. Saved eta=eta_center+sum(original_slope*((x-origin)-mean_offset)); this avoids large-origin cancellation. Raw intercept is also reported and may lose digits; use saved model for stable prediction. Unrepresentable raw coefficients/intercepts reject explicitly.
limitations.limits: Nominal n*(features+2)*q*maxiter*4<=200000000; per-group mode root<=100steps with<=60bracket expansions per side, line search<=50trials/step, eigen<=64sweeps. This preflight is not a cumulative CPU instruction cap. Finite-MLE LP<=4096Bland pivots and<=200M nominal tableau-cell updates,otherwise reject. LP constraints use row-normalized fixed design and |direction_j|<=1.
limitations.optimizer: Constrained local projected BFGS; coefficients standardized bounded[-30,30] as numerical guard; variance>=0 and<=variance_upper. A separate v0 GLM and three positive starts are compared. Coefficient/upper-variance bound prevents overall convergence.
limitations.quadrature: Fit uses requested odd q3..31; final likelihood,EB moments,saved posterior useq+4<=35. Compare total and each group LL differences; tolerance=max(user_tol,1e-8)*(1+abs(total_LL)),group tolerance=total_tolerance/G. This is order consistency,not a rigorous error bound. q15 can be insufficient,as recorded in evidence.
limitations.convergence: converged=optimizer_converged && quadrature_converged && !coefficient_guard_bound && !variance_upper_bound. Variance zero itself is a legitimate boundary optimum. Finite maxiter or failure may return convergedfalse.
limitations.uncertainty: Interior covariance inverts finite-difference joint integrated-likelihood Hessian in fixed coefficients/log1p variance; fixed block transformed to original units. At v0, exact fixed GLM information. Non-SPD/unrepresentable information gives null covariance/SE. Estimates/SE from unconverged fits remain diagnostic. No variance SE/pvalue.
limitations.portable_size: 7+3p+4G+2GQ<=16384doubles; fit caps p16,G200,Q35 ->14855. Variance-zero saves Q1. Prediction validates uniqueIDs,nonnegative variance/weights,unit weight sums within1e-8,and finite consistent moments; normalizes accepted weights.
limitations.prediction_semantics: conditional=known posterior-mean plug-in/new b0;posterior=known saved-posterior integral/new Gaussian-prior integral;population=Gaussian-prior integral for all. Logistic prior31/35consistency reported separately,not guaranteed for extreme variance.
limitations.JMP_differences: JMP19.2 supports more distributions,summarized trials,probit,random slopes/multiple factors/repeated structures and permits noninteger Poisson responses/unbounded variance options; absent here. Do not claim identical JMP defaults or full GLMM parity.
limitations.finite_mle_reference_inference: Bernoulli signed-X directions and Poisson directions unchanged on positive counts/nonincreasing on zero counts are standard GLM recession criteria. Their rejection in this random-intercept model follows because they improve conditional likelihood pointwise for every random intercept,thus also the positive Gaussian integral. This is a stated inference from the cited GLM theory,not a claim those papers establish full random-variance identification.

import json,math,pathlib,time
from datetime import datetime,timezone
import numpy as np
import scipy
from scipy import integrate,optimize,special

def group_integral(beta,variance,x,y,family,moments=False):
 eta=beta[0]+x@beta[1:]
 def cond(b):
  linear=eta+b
  if family=='binomial':return float(np.sum(y*linear-np.logaddexp(0,linear)))
  with np.errstate(over='ignore'):
   mu=np.exp(linear)
  return float(np.sum(y*linear-mu-special.gammaln(y+1)))
 if variance==0:return (cond(0),0.,0.,0.,0.) if moments else cond(0)
 def score(b):
  linear=eta+b
  with np.errstate(over='ignore'):
   mu=special.expit(linear) if family=='binomial' else np.exp(linear)
  return float(np.sum(y-mu)-b/variance)
 extent=max(1.,math.sqrt(variance));left=-extent;right=extent
 while score(left)<0:left*=2
 while score(right)>0:right*=2
 mode=optimize.brentq(score,left,right,xtol=1e-13,rtol=1e-14)
 mu=special.expit(eta+mode) if family=='binomial' else np.exp(eta+mode)
 curvature=1/variance+np.sum(mu*(1-mu) if family=='binomial' else mu)
 scale=1/math.sqrt(curvature)
 def logdensity(b):return cond(b)-.5*b*b/variance-.5*math.log(2*math.pi*variance)
 maximum=logdensity(mode)
 def weight(t):
  v=logdensity(mode+scale*t)-maximum
  return math.exp(v) if v>-745 else 0.
 denominator,error=integrate.quad(weight,-np.inf,np.inf,epsabs=1e-11,epsrel=1e-11,limit=300)
 ll=maximum+math.log(scale*denominator)
 if not moments:return ll
 first,e1=integrate.quad(lambda t:t*weight(t),-np.inf,np.inf,epsabs=1e-11,epsrel=1e-11,limit=300)
 second,e2=integrate.quad(lambda t:t*t*weight(t),-np.inf,np.inf,epsabs=1e-11,epsrel=1e-11,limit=300)
 mean=mode+scale*first/denominator;posterior_variance=scale*scale*(second/denominator-(first/denominator)**2)
 return ll,mean,mode,posterior_variance,max(error,e1,e2)

def fit(data,family):
 a=np.array(data,dtype=float);x=a[:,:-2];y=a[:,-2];groups=a[:,-1];unique=np.unique(groups);p=x.shape[1]
 def objective(theta):
  beta=theta[:-1];variance=math.expm1(theta[-1]);return -sum(group_integral(beta,variance,x[groups==g],y[groups==g],family) for g in unique)
 initial=np.zeros(p+2);initial[0]=0 if family=='binomial' else math.log(y.mean());initial[-1]=math.log(2)
 starts=[]
 for variance in [.25,1,4]:
  initial[-1]=math.log1p(variance)
  sol=optimize.minimize(objective,initial,method='Nelder-Mead',bounds=[(-20,20)]*(p+1)+[(0,math.log1p(100))],options={'xatol':1e-9,'fatol':1e-10,'maxiter':2000});starts.append(sol)
 best=min(starts,key=lambda s:s.fun);theta=best.x;beta=theta[:-1];variance=math.expm1(theta[-1]);post=[group_integral(beta,variance,x[groups==g],y[groups==g],family,True) for g in unique]
 return {'family':family,'data':data,'intercept':float(beta[0]),'coefficients':beta[1:].tolist(),'variance':variance,'log_likelihood':float(-best.fun),'optimizer_success':bool(best.success),'optimizer_message':str(best.message),'iterations':int(best.nit),'group_ids':unique.tolist(),'posterior_mean':[v[1] for v in post],'posterior_mode':[v[2] for v in post],'posterior_variance':[v[3] for v in post],'max_quad_estimated_error':max(v[4] for v in post)}

start=time.time();fixtures=[]
binary=[]
for g,s in enumerate([0,1,2,4,5,6]):
 for i in range(6):binary.append([float(i<s),float(g)])
fixtures.append(fit(binary,'binomial'));print('binary',fixtures[-1]['intercept'],fixtures[-1]['variance'],fixtures[-1]['log_likelihood'],flush=True)
rng=np.random.default_rng(20261022);poisson=[]
for g,b in enumerate([-1.,-.5,0.,.4,.8,1.2]):
 for x in [-1.,-.5,0.,.5,1.]:poisson.append([x,float(rng.poisson(np.exp(.4+.35*x+b))),float(g)])
fixtures.append(fit(poisson,'poisson'));print('poisson',fixtures[-1]['intercept'],fixtures[-1]['coefficients'],fixtures[-1]['variance'],fixtures[-1]['log_likelihood'],flush=True)
boundary_binary=[[float(i>=3),float(g)] for g in range(6) for i in range(6)]
fixtures.append({'family':'binomial','data':boundary_binary,'intercept':0.,'coefficients':[],'variance':0.,'log_likelihood':36*math.log(.5),'intercept_standard_error':1/3,'source':'closed-form repeated balanced Bernoulli groups'})
boundary_poisson=[[float(y),float(g)] for g in range(6) for y in [1,2,3,2]]
ll=sum(y*math.log(2)-2-special.gammaln(y+1) for y,g in boundary_poisson)
fixtures.append({'family':'poisson','data':boundary_poisson,'intercept':math.log(2),'coefficients':[],'variance':0.,'log_likelihood':float(ll),'intercept_standard_error':1/math.sqrt(48),'source':'closed-form identical repeated Poisson group means'})
result={'schema_version':1,'timestamp_utc':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'seed':20261022,'numpy':np.__version__,'scipy':scipy.__version__,'elapsed_seconds':time.time()-start,'method':'scipy.integrate.quad on posterior-mode and curvature rescaled real-line integrals; scipy.optimize.brentq mode roots; Nelder-Mead integrated likelihood optimization with3independentstarts','fixtures':fixtures}
pathlib.Path('/private/tmp/jmp-glmm-quad-fixtures.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n');print('written',len(fixtures),'fixtures in',time.time()-start,'seconds',flush=True)
